svg.title: DBOS's words and this store's
svg.desc: Two panels. The upper one holds the two words that mean different things in the two vocabularies — "step" and "workflow" — each shown as one word over two meanings rather than as a mapping, because a mapping is what the panel exists to deny: in DBOS a step is a checkpointed unit inside a workflow, and here it is a declared unit of work a participant performs. The lower panel is the rest of the vocabulary, each DBOS name paired by an arrow with what it is called here: queue, partition key, executor, client, system database, send and receive, events, listen queues, migration and workflow id. Beneath both, the names that have no counterpart in either direction.

g.text: TWO FALSE FRIENDS, AND THE REST OF THE VOCABULARY
One word, two meanings — these are the ones that bite

text.tspan: a checkpointed unit inside a workflow, replayed rather
a declared unit of work a participant performs,
nothing is called one. A verb a door serves, or one fleet

g.text: Both spellings are live in one file: a door runs a lane verb as a DBOS step, and the verb it is serving is about a dbo step.
AND THE NAMES THAT MAP CLEANLY
a tenant's durable layer, a door, or a consumer
the joiner's writer: offers, consumes nothing
an ask on the stream, lane to door
the door's answer, and the wake-up
the durable bootstrap a substrate carries
No counterpart either way: DBOS has no tenant, participant, enrolment or register — it carries them as opaque strings. This store has no DBOS step and does not expose one.
